## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up at `97671612` to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12753#issuecomment-5788138285) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12753#issuecomment-5789613983). The per-adapter block failure finding is **resolved**. No new issue was found in this commit.

**Verified:** [`block_adapters()`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/97671612707ceded786232955465d68e50a6ba59/bin/omarchy-bluetooth-power#L74-L91) now attempts every listed HCI adapter, returns nonzero if any block fails, and returns the type-wide fallback's own status when no adapter is listed. Results through the real helper with synthetic `rfkill`/`bluetoothctl` backends:

```text
Helper exit status                          base   8af094e3   97671612
off, listing allowed, blocking denied         1        0          1
powered toggle, same condition                1        0          1
off, two adapters, first ID fails             0        0          1   (both IDs attempted)
off, no HCI adapter, fallback exits 3         3        3          3
```

(Base exits 0 in the two-adapter row because it issues one type-wide block, which the synthetic model lets succeed.)

The util-linux source matches the modeled condition: `rfkill` opens `/dev/rfkill` read-only to list and read-write to block, and exits nonzero when that open fails. The new test case fails with the `8af094e3` helper and passes at `97671612`. HCI-only selection still holds, with the platform switch never blocked, including with two adapters. The no-adapter fallback is unchanged.

**Author's "whole bluetooth file green":** the shell section of `test/shell.d/bluetooth-test.sh` passes in full. Its Node section (panel files, unchanged by this PR) was not run.

**Optional test improvement:** the new case uses one adapter and fails every block. Three altered helpers still pass it: one that stops at the first failure, one that escalates a failure to `rfkill block bluetooth` (which would trip the platform switch), and one whose fallback returns 0. A two-adapter listing where only one ID fails, asserting both IDs are attempted and no `rfkill block bluetooth` is issued, would catch the first two. A platform-only listing with a failing block would catch the third.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned source review of `97671612` and the relevant util-linux and systemd source, plus isolated checks with synthetic `rfkill`/`bluetoothctl` backends (the shell section of the bluetooth test and a base/`8af094e3`/`97671612` status matrix). No physical radio, real `/dev/rfkill` permissions, firmware, UI, reboot or suspend/resume validation.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh (source review and isolated synthetic runs) and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh (source-only) technical assessments of this follow-up, and an Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
